privacy.collect.session_data: Your uploaded CSV and JSON files, analysis snapshots, report subjects and the session identifier that ties them to your browser
privacy.collect.session_src: You, while using the web app
privacy.collect.assistant_data: The messages you send, the recent conversation, and a structured description of the current screen state
privacy.collect.assistant_src: You, when you use the assistant
privacy.collect.drive_data: An OAuth access and refresh token, and the identifier of the Drive folder you selected
privacy.collect.community_data: The name, affiliation and review text you type into the review form
privacy.collect.technical_data: IP address, request time, requested path, HTTP status and user-agent string in server logs; IP-keyed counters used for rate limiting
privacy.collect.no_trackers: We do not run advertising trackers, third-party analytics scripts, social pixels, session replay or fingerprinting on this website.
privacy.why.h: Why we process it, and on what basis
privacy.why.account_purpose: Create and run your account; verify your address; let you reset a password
privacy.why.account_basis: Performance of our agreement with you
privacy.why.analysis_purpose: Run the analysis you asked for and hold your files for the session
privacy.why.analysis_basis: Performance of our agreement with you
privacy.why.seats_purpose: Issue, bind and check licence seats; enforce the one-machine limit; apply revocations
privacy.why.seats_basis: Performance of our agreement; our legitimate interest in protecting the Service from unlicensed use
privacy.why.assistant_basis: Performance of our agreement with you
privacy.why.drive_purpose: Synchronise your files to your own Drive folder
privacy.why.drive_data: Google Drive tokens and folder ID
privacy.why.drive_basis: Your consent, given at the Google authorisation screen
privacy.why.reviews_purpose: Consider a review for publication on the home page
privacy.why.reviews_basis: Your consent, given by submitting the form
privacy.why.uptime_purpose: Keep the Service up: debugging, abuse prevention, rate limiting, security investigation
privacy.why.uptime_basis: Our legitimate interest in a secure, available service
privacy.why.legal_purpose: Comply with a legal obligation or respond to a lawful request
privacy.why.withdraw: Where a purpose rests on consent, you can withdraw it at any time — disconnect Drive from the Drive panel or from your Google account settings, or email us to have a published review taken down. Withdrawal does not affect processing already carried out.
privacy.never.b1: We do not sell, rent or trade your personal data or your measurement data.
privacy.never.b2: We do not use your measurement data, your files or your reports to train any machine-learning model, ours or anyone else's.
privacy.never.b3: We do not build advertising or marketing profiles, and we send no marketing email. The only email we send is transactional: verification, password reset, and licensing notices.
privacy.never.b4: We do not read your files for any purpose other than running the computation you requested — except where we must access a specific record to investigate a support request you raised or a security incident.
privacy.never.b5: We do not store your password. We store only a bcrypt hash, which we cannot reverse.
privacy.desktop.p1: The desktop build of Easy OKAPI is local-first. It runs a server on your own machine, reads the folders you point it at, and talks to the colorimeter over a USB serial port. Your measurement data is never uploaded to us as part of normal operation.
privacy.desktop.stays_b1: Every CSV, calibration JSON, report and export you create.
privacy.desktop.stays_b2: An interaction event log under log/events/, written as one JSONL file per session. It records which actions were taken and when, so that a bug can be reconstructed. It is stored locally and is never transmitted automatically.
privacy.desktop.stays_b3: Your application settings and the activation file.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b1: Activation and licence checks. The application sends your licence token and the machine's hardware fingerprint to our server when you activate, and periodically thereafter so a revoked seat or banned account takes effect. Nothing else about the machine is sent.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b2: The hardware fingerprint itself is a SHA-256 digest of a stable operating-system machine identifier (the Windows MachineGuid, the macOS IOPlatformUUID, or the Linux machine-id) combined with a fixed salt. We receive only the digest. It identifies a machine to us, but it is not reversible and it carries no name, serial number, MAC address, location or hardware inventory.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b3: Update checks and downloads, which send the licence token so we can confirm your seat before serving a build.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b4: Assistant messages, only when you use the assistant — see §06.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b5: Bug reports, only when you send one. The application prepares a zip of the event log files you select and opens a draft email; you decide whether to attach it and whether to send.
privacy.desktop.leaves_b6: Background music lookups, if you use that feature, resolve stream metadata over the network. No data about your work is included.
privacy.desktop.uninstall: Uninstalling the application removes it from your machine. To also remove the machine's seat from our records, delete your account or email us.
privacy.assistant.c1_before: When you use the assistant, your prompt, the recent conversation and a structured summary of the current screen are sent to
privacy.assistant.c1_after: , which runs the language model and returns the reply. This applies both to the web application and to the desktop application when it uses our proxy.
privacy.assistant.c2: Anything you type into the assistant leaves your machine. Do not paste personal data, patient identifiers, credentials or confidential third-party information into it.
privacy.assistant.c3: We do not use your conversations to train a model. Groq's own handling of the request is governed by their terms and privacy policy.
privacy.assistant.c4: In the desktop application you may configure your own provider API key. Requests then go from your machine directly to that provider and never reach our servers.
privacy.assistant.c5: If you rate an assistant answer, the rating and the exchange it refers to may be stored so we can find and fix bad answers.
privacy.drive.c1: Connecting Google Drive is optional and off by default. The connection is made through Google's own OAuth screen, which shows you exactly what you are granting before you agree.
privacy.drive.c2: The connection requests Drive access together with your basic profile and email address, so that files can be written to and read back from the folder you choose and so we can show you which account is connected.
privacy.drive.c3: We use the authorisation only to push your Easy OKAPI session files to the folder you select, and to pull them back when you ask. We do not index, scan or copy the rest of your Drive.
privacy.drive.c4: We store the OAuth tokens and the selected folder ID so the connection survives a page reload. Tokens are held encrypted at rest.
privacy.drive.c5_before: You can disconnect at any time from the Drive panel, or revoke our access entirely at
privacy.drive.c5_after: . Files already synchronised stay in your Drive, under your control — disconnecting does not delete them.
privacy.drive.c6_before: Our use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the
privacy.drive.c6_link: Google API Services User Data Policy
privacy.cookies.intro: We use no advertising or analytics cookies. What the site sets is limited to what it needs to work:
privacy.cookies.session_purpose: A signed cookie holding your session identifier and sign-in state. Set with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Lasts up to 30 days, and is also subject to an idle timeout.
privacy.cookies.theme_purpose: Remembers whether you chose the light or dark interface. Stays in your browser, never sent to us. Clearing site data removes it.
privacy.cookies.lang_purpose: Remembers the interface language you picked, so the site opens in it next time. Holds a language code only, such as "vi". Lasts one year; clearing site data removes it.
privacy.cookies.landing: The landing page opens no session storage at all: a visitor who never enters the web application creates no server-side record beyond an ordinary request log line.
privacy.processors.intro: We use the following providers to run the Service. Each processes data only as needed to provide its part.
privacy.processors.heroku_role: Hosting, PostgreSQL database, Redis session and rate-limit store
privacy.processors.drive_role: File synchronisation, if you connect it
privacy.processors.drive_sees: The files you synchronise, in your own Drive
privacy.processors.oauth_role: Social sign-in, if you use it
privacy.processors.oauth_sees: That you signed in to Easy OKAPI
privacy.processors.smtp_sees: Your email address and the message content
privacy.processors.groq_sees: Your assistant messages and screen context
privacy.processors.disclosure_before: Beyond these, we disclose personal data only where we must: to comply with a law or a valid legal request, to enforce our
privacy.processors.disclosure_after: , or to protect the rights and safety of users or the public. If the Service is ever transferred to another operator within HCMUS–VNU, account records may transfer with it, and we will tell you before that happens.
privacy.transfers.p1: CBBiotec is in Vietnam, but the Service runs on infrastructure operated by providers based in the United States and hosted in their regions. Using the Service therefore involves transferring your data outside Vietnam and, if you are in the EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland, outside those areas.
privacy.transfers.p2: We rely on our providers' standard contractual clauses and equivalent transfer mechanisms for those transfers, and we keep the data transferred to what the Service actually needs. If you would rather your measurement data did not leave your own machine at all, use the desktop application rather than the hosted web application (§05).
privacy.retention.account_kept: Until you delete your account, or until we delete it after a long period of inactivity or following a ban
privacy.retention.tokens_kept: 24 hours and 1 hour respectively; cleared once used
privacy.retention.social_kept: Until you disconnect them or delete your account
privacy.retention.seats_kept: Until the seat is revoked or the account is deleted
privacy.retention.session_kept: For the life of the session, up to the 30-day session lifetime; cleared earlier when you sign out or clear the session
privacy.retention.assistant_kept: Held for the conversation; not retained as a durable transcript by us, except where you submitted feedback on an answer
privacy.retention.ratelimit_kept: Minutes to hours — only as long as the limit window
privacy.retention.logs_kept: A short rolling window kept by the hosting platform, then discarded
privacy.retention.reviews_kept: In our mailbox until handled; if published, until you ask us to remove it
privacy.retention.longer: Where we must keep something longer to resolve a dispute, meet a legal obligation or prevent recurring abuse, we keep only that, and only for as long as the reason lasts.
privacy.security.b1: All traffic to the Service is over HTTPS.
privacy.security.b2: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Plaintext passwords are never written to the database or to logs.
privacy.security.b3: The session cookie is signed and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, so it cannot be read by page scripts or sent cross-site.
privacy.security.b4: Permanent activation tokens are RS256-signed and verified against a public key held in the client, so a forged token fails verification offline.
privacy.security.b5: Google credentials and OAuth tokens are stored encrypted at rest.
privacy.security.b6: Account, download, activation and assistant endpoints are rate-limited to blunt credential stuffing, mail flooding and cost-drain attacks.
privacy.security.b7: Access to production data is limited to the maintainers who need it to run the Service.
privacy.security.p1_before: No system is perfectly secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. If we become aware of a breach affecting your personal data, we will notify you and the relevant authority where the law requires it. If you find a vulnerability, please report it to
privacy.security.p1_after: before disclosing it publicly — we will work with you.
privacy.rights.h: Your rights, and how to use them
privacy.rights.intro: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access a copy of your data, to correct it, to have it deleted, to restrict or object to processing, to portability, and to withdraw a consent you gave. We apply these to every user, wherever you are.
privacy.rights.c1: Do it yourself. Your name and email are editable from the account settings panel. You can delete your account there too, with password confirmation — that removes your account record, your social sign-in connections and your machine seats. You can disconnect Google Drive from the Drive panel.
privacy.rights.c2_after: with "Privacy request" in the subject. We will confirm your identity through the email address on the account and answer within 30 days.
privacy.rights.c3: Exercising these rights is free. If a request is manifestly unfounded or repetitive we may decline it, and we will tell you why.
privacy.rights.c4: Deleting your account is irreversible and immediately disables every activated machine seat. Export the files you want to keep first.
privacy.rights.c5: If you are unhappy with how we handled a request, tell us first so we can put it right. You also have the right to complain to your local data protection authority, and in Vietnam to the competent authority for personal data protection.
privacy.children.p1_before: The Service is not directed at children and we do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 16, or under the minimum age of digital consent where they live, whichever is higher. If you believe a child has given us personal data, write to
privacy.children.p2: Where Easy OKAPI is used in undergraduate or secondary-school teaching, the supervising institution is responsible for obtaining any consent its own rules require.
privacy.changes.p1: We will update this policy when the Service changes. The version number and effective date at the top of this page always identify the current text. For a change that materially affects how we use data you have already given us, we will notify you by email or in the application at least 14 days before it takes effect, unless a shorter period is required by law or by a security issue.
landing.page_title: Easy OKAPI — Open-colorimeter Kinetics Analysis Platform
landing.meta_description: Easy OKAPI reads Open Colorimeter runs, fits the kinetics, builds the standard curve and writes the report, in the browser or offline on your bench machine.
landing.og_title: Easy OKAPI — Open-colorimeter Kinetics Analysis Platform
landing.og_description: Kinetics, endpoint, calibration and reporting for colorimetric assays. Run it in the browser or install it next to the instrument.
landing.hero.h1: From cuvette to standard curve in one app.
landing.hero.lede: Easy OKAPI reads your colorimeter runs, fits the kinetics, builds the calibration and writes the report. Open it in a browser, or install it next to the instrument and work offline.
landing.spec.channels_v: up to 4, set by the instrument
landing.readout.plot_aria: Absorbance rising over twelve minutes and levelling off, with the maximum-rate window marked
landing.readout.caption: Fig. 1 — Absorbance at {band} nm over {tmax} min, {assay}. Shaded: sliding-window interval of maximum rate; dashed: fitted tangent, R² = {r2}; dotted: saturation plateau A(sat) = {sat} AU.
landing.watch.p: Six minutes on a real assay: capture on the colorimeter, the kinetics fit, the standard curve, and the report that comes out the other end.
landing.modes.h: Pick the mode and the fit follows.
landing.modes.p: The same files carry through every mode. Switch from a raw trace to a fitted standard curve to a printable report without exporting anything in between.
landing.modes.kinetics_p: Sliding-window regression across the whole trace, with the annotation lines drawn on the chart.
landing.modes.point_p: Read a single time point across every source, with baseline subtraction when you need to compare channels directly.
landing.modes.calibrate_p: Fit known concentrations against any kinetics quantity or time point, then keep the coefficients as a reusable JSON file.
landing.modes.report_p: Group saved analysis snapshots into subjects, reorder them, and publish the set in one pass.
landing.workflow.p: The desktop build drives the colorimeter itself, so a run goes from the cuvette to the finished report without leaving the app or re-typing a number.
landing.workflow.connect_p: Plug the colorimeter in over USB. The app reads its mode, active channels, live value and battery, and gives you a keypad to drive the menu without touching the device.
landing.workflow.record_p: Start a session with your own folder and filename. Readings land on the chart as they arrive — pause, resume, or take a manual point reading mid-run.
landing.workflow.analyse_p: Chart absorbance against time, zoom to a window, set the sliding-window size, and read the kinetics for each source.
landing.workflow.calibrate_p: Fit your standards with the regression that suits the chemistry, check R², and export the coefficients.
landing.workflow.derive_p: Load a saved curve and every measured value is converted to concentration next to its own analysis panel.
landing.workflow.report_p: Push snapshots into named subjects and publish the lot as HTML or an Excel workbook with charts.
landing.workflow.note: Connect and Record need the desktop build, because a browser tab cannot reach a USB device. From Analyse onwards the web app does the same work on files you already have.
landing.caps.h: Built around how a bench actually runs.
landing.caps.disk_p: Everything lands in one folder — by default under your Documents, and movable to an external drive from App Settings. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
landing.caps.csv_p: Create, rename, copy, move, merge and edit CSVs and their folders without leaving the app or opening a file manager.
landing.caps.sources_p: Each measurement channel gets its own chart. Split by source, filter by source count, or normalise them all to baseline.
landing.caps.models_p: Linear, polynomial, logarithmic, exponential and Michaelis–Menten, with an R² threshold to drop poor windows.
landing.caps.formulas_p: Exported workbooks carry the fitted curve as a real Excel formula, so a value typed into the sheet returns its concentration.
landing.caps.assistant_p: Ask about your data, your coefficients or the interface. It answers, or walks you through the app step by step. This is the one feature that needs an internet connection; everything else works without one.
landing.caps.note: The interface speaks English, Tiếng Việt, 中文 (简体), Français, 日本語, Русский and 한국어. Theme, default mode, time and concentration units and sort order are remembered between launches, and an update installs over the top without touching your data, reports or settings.
landing.run.h: In the browser, or beside the instrument.
landing.run.p: Both builds run the same analysis. The desktop build adds direct device control, which a browser tab cannot do.
landing.run.web_p: Open a tab, drop your files in, and work. An account keeps your session files and lets you sync to Drive.
landing.run.web_b1: Full kinetics, point, calibrate and report modes
landing.run.no_account_after: to keep your files between sessions.
landing.run.desktop_p: Install Easy OKAPI on the bench machine to drive the device and analyse the run in the same place, with no network in the loop.
landing.run.desktop_b1: Direct device control and live capture
landing.run.desktop_b4: Activated with a download token from your account
landing.run.signed_in_note: Signed in as {name}. Your download token is in the web app, under Get Offline Version.
landing.closing.h: Your data stays where you put it.
landing.closing.p: Install the desktop build and the whole analysis runs offline, on the machine beside the instrument, in a folder you choose.

a11y.meta_description: How Easy OKAPI conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, what is known not to conform, and how to report an accessibility barrier.
a11y.title: Accessibility Statement
a11y.lede: CBBiotec is committed to making Easy OKAPI usable by every researcher, including those who work with assistive technology. This statement records what we target, what we have measured, and what is still broken.
a11y.commitment.callout: Easy OKAPI aims to conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Where it does not yet, the gap is listed below rather than left unsaid.
a11y.commitment.p1: Easy OKAPI is companion software for a laboratory instrument: it is used for hours at a stretch, often in poor light, sometimes by people who cannot use a mouse. Accessibility is treated as part of whether the tool works at all, not as a finishing touch.
a11y.commitment.p2: This statement applies to the web application at www.easyokapi.cbbiotec.vn, to the public and legal pages on the same domain, and to the downloadable desktop application together with its installers.
a11y.standard.p1: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) define requirements for making digital content more accessible. Easy OKAPI is measured against WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
a11y.standard.c1: Conformance claim: the web application and the public pages are partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Partially conformant means that most of the content meets the standard, and that the parts which do not are named under Known limitations below.
a11y.standard.c2: Related standards: WCAG 2.2 Level AA contains everything in WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which is the technical requirement referenced by EN 301 549 in the European Union and by Section 508 of the US Rehabilitation Act. Work done for this claim therefore serves those requirements too.
a11y.standard.c3: Not claimed: Level AAA. A few AAA criteria — sign-language alternatives for media, for instance — are beyond what a research tool of this size can sustain honestly.
a11y.standard.p2: Charts, calibration curves and exported reports are numeric content. A chart drawn on a <canvas> cannot be read by assistive technology, so the same numbers are published as a data table beside every chart.
a11y.scope.b1: the web application — data display, calibration, reporting, the file and coefficient tables, and the assistant;
a11y.scope.b2: the public pages — the home page, the Terms of Service, the Privacy Policy, this statement and the contact form;
a11y.scope.b3: the account pages — sign-up, sign-in, e-mail verification and password reset;
a11y.scope.b4: the desktop application and the macOS, Windows and Linux installers.
a11y.scope.p2: It does not cover third-party services reached from Easy OKAPI: Google Drive, the sign-in screens of Google and GitHub, or the publisher pages of cited articles. Those are governed by their own providers' accessibility statements.
a11y.measures.p1: The following are standing commitments, kept in the codebase rather than in a policy document:
a11y.measures.b1: Keyboard operation. Every control can be reached and operated with a keyboard alone, in a sensible order, with a focus indicator that is never suppressed.
a11y.measures.b2: Names and roles. Every control carries a text name — icon-only and emoji-only buttons have a hidden label — and every collapsible section reports whether it is open or closed.
a11y.measures.b3: Status messages. Errors, synchronisation results and analysis outcomes are announced to assistive technology without stealing focus from what you are doing.
a11y.measures.b4: Contrast and colour. Text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio (3:1 for large text), interface borders and focus rings meet 3:1, and colour is never the only way a piece of information is conveyed.
a11y.measures.b5: Motion and timing. Animation is suppressed when the operating system asks for reduced motion. The only time limit in the product is the 60-minute inactivity sign-out, which is a security control and can be extended on request.
a11y.measures.b6: Zoom and reflow. The interface stays usable at 200% zoom and down to a 320-pixel viewport, and tolerates text spacing imposed by the reader.
a11y.measures.b7: Language. The interface, the legal documents and this statement are published in seven languages, each declaring its language in the markup so that a screen reader speaks it with the right voice.
a11y.compat.p1: Easy OKAPI is built to work with current assistive technology. These are the combinations we test:
a11y.compat.caption: Tested screen reader and browser combinations, by platform
a11y.compat.p2: The web application needs JavaScript and a browser released within roughly the last three years; it is not designed for Internet Explorer. On a phone the analysis screens are usable but cramped — for a long session, the desktop application or a tablet is the better experience.
a11y.limits.callout: The following are known not to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA. They are published deliberately; each one is tracked, and each one has a workaround.
a11y.limits.p1: As at the date of this statement:
a11y.limits.c1: Interactive charts. Zooming and panning a chart with a pointer has no keyboard equivalent. Workaround: the data table under each chart carries every plotted value, and the display range can be set numerically in the From and To fields.
a11y.limits.c2: Excel and PDF exports. Generated report files are not tagged for accessibility — an exported workbook has no table headers marked up for a screen reader. Workaround: the same figures are readable in the application before export, and we will supply a plain-text or CSV version of any report on request.
a11y.limits.c3: The assistant's transcript. Answers are streamed and announced in fragments as they arrive, which is verbose with a screen reader. Workaround: the finished answer can be re-read as a single block once streaming stops.
a11y.limits.c4: Third-party dialogues. Some confirmation dialogues come from a third-party library (SweetAlert2) whose focus handling we do not fully control. Workaround: every destructive action confirmed in such a dialogue can be cancelled with the Escape key.
a11y.limits.c5: Content contributed by others. Reviews and citations submitted by other researchers are published as written; we cannot guarantee the structure or the reading level of text we did not write. Workaround: every review is read by a person before it is published, and any entry reported as unreadable is rewritten or withdrawn — tell us which one.
a11y.installers.p1: The desktop application ships with a graphical installer on each platform. Those are native applications rather than web pages, so they are assessed against the software clauses of EN 301 549, and against WCAG 2.2 Level AA wherever a criterion applies to software.
a11y.installers.b1: Keyboard. Every installer step can be completed with the keyboard alone: Tab moves between controls, Space and Enter activate them, Escape cancels. Nothing depends on a drag or on a pointer gesture.
a11y.installers.b2: Screen readers. Installer windows expose a window title, a labelled control for every field and button, and progress as text rather than only as a moving bar. The Windows installer is checked with Narrator and NVDA, the macOS installer with VoiceOver, the Linux installer with Orca.
a11y.installers.b3: No time limits. No installer step expires or advances on its own, and the splash screen is informational only — it never takes focus away from what you are doing.
a11y.installers.b4: A non-graphical path exists. Every platform can be installed from the command line without the graphical installer at all. That is the most reliable route with a screen reader, and the one we recommend if the graphical installer gives trouble.
a11y.installers.p2: The command-line instructions for each platform ship with the download and are repeated on the download page. If you cannot complete an installation with assistive technology, write to us: we will walk you through it or provide a pre-configured build.
a11y.assessment.p1: This statement was prepared by CBBiotec on the basis of a self-assessment. It has not been audited by an external body; had it been, the body and the date would be named here.
a11y.assessment.b1: a manual keyboard-only walkthrough of every screen, following the documented task flows;
a11y.assessment.b2: screen-reader testing on the combinations listed above;
a11y.assessment.b3: automated checks that run with the test suite, so that a change removing a landmark, a form label or the skip link fails the build.
a11y.assessment.p2: Automated checks catch roughly a third of what matters. They are a floor, not the assessment.
a11y.feedback.p1: If you meet a barrier in Easy OKAPI — anything you cannot do, or can only do with difficulty, because of the way the software is built — please tell us. A barrier report is treated as a defect report, not as a feature request.
a11y.feedback.p2: We aim to acknowledge an accessibility report within 5 working days and to provide a remedy or a dated plan within 20 working days. If a fix will take longer than that, we will say so and offer a workaround in the meantime.
a11y.feedback.p3: If you need any part of Easy OKAPI or its documentation in another format — large print, plain text, an accessible spreadsheet — ask, and we will provide it at no charge.
a11y.enforcement.p1: If our response does not satisfy you, say so in a reply: the report is then escalated within CBBiotec to the project lead at the University of Science (HCMUS–VNU), who will answer in writing.
a11y.enforcement.p2: Easy OKAPI is published from Vietnam and is not a public-sector body of an EU member state or of the United States, so no statutory enforcement procedure applies to it. We hold ourselves to the response times above regardless. This statement is reviewed at least once a year, and whenever a substantial change is made to the software.
